name: Sudip Paudel
headline: I write the layer most people import.
summary: Register-level firmware on ARM Cortex-M4, synthesised SystemVerilog on FPGA, and two platforms running in production. Computer Engineering at UT Arlington.
about: I build things that sit on both sides of the hardware/software line. On the metal side that means register-level drivers with no vendor HAL — configuring clocks, timers, NVIC and UART directly out of the datasheet — and synthesizable SystemVerilog on FPGA, where a design isn't done until static timing says it is.

On the software side it means shipping. I've designed, built and deployed two production AI platforms end to end: data model and row-level-security auth, the product surface, and the deploy pipeline. Same instinct in both worlds — understand the layer underneath instead of trusting the abstraction.
I'm studying Computer Engineering at UT Arlington. I'm open to engineering internships and roles where I can work close to the hardware, the systems, or both.
